question: Can the existing legal benchmark that encodes temporal validity (LEGAL-LINK-EU) be extended or re-labelled to version-level retrieval evaluation, which would pre-empt the proposed benchmark resource?
description: The closest legal resource already encodes temporal validity and normative relationships with authoritative reference context. If its released data or corpus can be re-labelled to identify the clause version in force at a query date, it could be extended into a version-level benchmark, which would further reduce the benchmark contribution to the measurement design alone.
confidence_basis: Full-text evidence on how the closest legal benchmark's items are constructed and what its grounding axis supplies, plus the same paper's explicit statement that retrieval-oriented legal benchmarks do not assess in-force status of retrieved provisions. Residual doubt is about whether an unreleased extended split exists.
rationale: Its questions already depend on temporal scope and normativity, so the marginal work to add version-identity labels may be small; whether it evaluates retrieval of a specific version is currently unknown from the abstract-level record.
resolution: Resolved: the closest legal benchmark does not pre-empt the proposed resource. Its items are multiple-choice questions with answer-option gold labels generated from pairs of EUR-Lex document passages and their relations, and its grounding axis supplies authoritative reference context instead of requiring a retriever to choose among candidate versions. Turning it into a version-level retrieval benchmark would require new construction (version chains, per-clause in-force intervals, version-identity labels over a candidate pool), not a re-labelling. The same paper states that retrieval-oriented legal benchmarks assume a normatively stable corpus and do not assess whether retrieved provisions remain in force, and that current architectures lack the temporal logic to determine this - evidence that the temporal-validity dimension of legal retrieval is acknowledged as unmeasured. The remaining requirement is a corpus with clause-level validity metadata of the EUR-Lex kind.
